verdicts.correction: The log lines match the quotes exactly, and 61 of the last 61 Player logs contain 'waitForNewPlayerProcess new waiting for mutex result is 0X000000'. One detail weakens the handover story. The new client (DDC69) logged WAIT_ABANDONED (0X000080) at 18:47:36.500Z. The old client (10630) only logged EventWaitResultUpdate at 18:47:36.688Z, and it was still alive until about .93. So the abandoned owner was not the old client exiting. The mutex is probably taken and released briefly, or by some other thread. How the mutex is used remains unknown. The second line in the new log returned 0X000000 in the same millisecond.

Every date checks out against the GitHub API: Dashbloxx 95d6020c on 2023-06-12, Bloxstrap d244f42b on 2025-03-15, 1a63b597 on 2025-09-30, the v2.10.0 notes on 2025-10-01, Bloxstrap #5579 on 2025-07-28 and #5635 on 2025-08-05. RAM is archived (last push 2024-10-01). MultiBloxy uses new Mutex(false, "ROBLOX_singletonEvent"), so it does not take ownership. evanovar's _MR_SINGLETON_NAMES are exactly "ROBLOX_SingletonEvent", "ROBLOX_singletonEvent" and "ROBLOX_singletonMutex", created with CreateMutexW(None, True, name).

Two details are wrong:
(f) Bloxstrap #6054 literally says "creating a mutex called ROBLOX_SingletonEvent", with a capital S and E. Microsoft's CreateMutexW docs say "Name comparison is case sensitive", and a local PowerShell test confirmed it: TryOpenExisting with different case returned False. So that exact name would not collide with the client's ROBLOX_singletonEvent. The reporter also held the old ROBLOX_singletonMutex and was unsure which one mattered. #6054 is therefore weak evidence. It was closed 'not planned' by bluepilledgreat on 2026-04-02.
(i) MultiAlt's singleton.rs has no test named a_reserved_name_cannot_be_created_as_an_event. The closest is a_wrong_type_object_of_the_same_name_does_not_block_the_next_client, which asserts that open_event_failure_blocks(ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE) is false.

The type-mismatch behaviour itself was reproduced locally: with a mutex holding the name, creating an EventWaitHandle of the same name throws 'A WaitHandle of a different type might have the same name'.

The timeline is also messier than stated. DevForum 2324412 (May 2023) shows multi-client working with only ROBLOX_singletonMutex held, Dashbloxx switched to the event name a month later, yet Bloxstrap's mutex-only method still worked from March to about July 2025.

'Works today' rests on maintained tools (evanovar, MultiAlt) and is not independently confirmed.

The core claims hold. MultiBloxy's PerformAction("Fix") calls HandleCloser.CloseAllHandles(). evanovar returns ROBLOX_RUNNING in both modes. MultiAlt's docs say the mutex method "só resolve se o app pegar o mutex antes de qualquer cliente subir" (it only works if the app takes the mutex before any client starts), and its singleton.rs says OpenProcess(PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE) works without elevation. Bloxstrap's LaunchHandler.cs still has the ConfirmLaunches && Mutex.TryOpenExisting("ROBLOX_singletonMutex") check.

The Fishstrap detail is wrong. Fishstrap's LaunchHandler.cs has no ROBLOX_singleton reference. Its ConfirmLaunches gate calls Utilities.IsRobloxRunning(), which compares process names. Its own mutexes are "{ProjectName}-Bootstrapper" (Bootstrapper.cs) and "{ProjectName}-BackgroundUpdater" (LaunchHandler.cs).

The July and September sequences match the logs. In 20260720T162120Z, at 16:26:34.255 'Successfully launched new process in systray mode' is followed by EventWaitResultUpdate and then shutDown. The 8A4E8 log shows 'Systray initialized in sync mode', a mutex result of 0X000000 and background update timers. In 0.739 30D25 the tray process lived from 08:42:48 to 09:01:28 on 2026-09-20.

Three corrections:
(1) Since 2026-09-20 there has been no tray spawn. None of the 40 most recent Player logs (all of October 2026) contains 'launched new process in systray mode', although every one logs 'Tray treatment is ON' and 38 log 'Auto startup is enabled'. So closing the window does not always spawn a tray process.
(2) The auto-start location can be found. The exe contains, in UTF-16, "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" next to the value name "RobloxPlayerBeta", and also a UTF-16 "--launch-to-tray". Locally, HKCU\...\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run has a RobloxPlayerBeta entry marked disabled (03) at 2026-07-22 22:31 UTC, and the Run value itself is now absent. So a tray process can start at logon through HKCU Run\RobloxPlayerBeta. That its command line contains --launch-to-tray is still inferred.
(3) The cited Sept log 0.737.100.7371443_20260917T111708Z_Player_D7A87 does not show the spawn pattern. It shows the user clicking 'Systray menu item Exit' in the in-game client.
sources: local static scan of RobloxPlayerBeta.exe 0.744 (UTF-16 at 0x71531f6 and 0x7153220)

verdicts.correction:
Local files match. RobloxCookies.dat is 2,351 bytes of JSON with keys CookiesVersion='1' and CookiesData (a string). The appStorage.json keys match, and both files were modified at 2026-10-24 01:00 local. LocalStorage also holds memProfStorage<number>.json files, one created at each launch.

The evanovar locking code is confirmed: CreateFile(GENERIC_READ, share 0, OPEN_ALWAYS), then msvcrt.locking LK_NBLCK over 0x7fffffff bytes, on both files. niccsprojects PR #47 (2026-04-09) opens RobloxCookies.dat with share mode 0 to fix teleport error 773, and creating no773fix.txt turns that off. DevForum 2324412 (2023-05-08) does say '773 and 512 (Unauthorized)'. MultiBloxy #3 (2024-12-08) reports 773 for every client except the last one opened. Bloxstrap #5841 (2025-09-20) is confirmed.

Two nuances:
(1) evanovar #83 happened in Handle64 mode, which closes handles inside the client and is a different path from RoALT's. Its reporter closed it themselves as completed, and no maintainer replied.
(2) #85 (2026-10-13) is an investigation, not a fix. The wrong displayed name 'remained absent while the original file was held exclusively', and the issue says this says nothing about which credentials the CAPTCHA used.

Roblox did make an official statement. The DevForum post 'An Update on Automated Action Against Modified Clients' (topic 3640609) was posted 2025-05-06 by the official 'Roblox' account (staff=true), with its FAQ updated 2025-05-08. The FAQ asks: 'Does this affect tools that allow you to run multiple clients on the same machine such as ones that remove the client's "window" cap or tools like Multiple Games?'. The answer: 'If the method you are using to run multiple clients does not modify the client binary, then this change will not impact your workflow.' It goes on: 'While we do not officially support running multiple player clients simultaneously, we noted your feedback around the value in running multiple clients for testing and development, and we will investigate providing an officially-supported solution.'

The same post defines modified clients as including 'running instances of the official version of Roblox modified by external tools at runtime', with action 'up to and including account termination'. RoALT's approach (a mutex created in its own process, with no writes into the client) fits the 'does not modify the client binary' case. Handle-closing tools are a grey area.

The rest of M7 checks out. DevForum 2324412: ScipioAfrikanos, 2023-05-11, staff=false, no title. 3730867: created 2025-06-13, last post 2026-08-22, no staff replies. Ban API and alt detection: topic 3039740, 2024-06-25, posted by Roblox with staff=true. Bloxstrap #5890 (2025-10-01) says 'an anticheat mechanism that closes the instance after a bit'. The 'autoclicked' quote is not in the issue body; it may be in a comment, which was not checked.

Registry reads match exactly. The roblox-player and roblox keys both point to "...\version-9ac8595712b447a7\RobloxPlayerBeta.exe" %1. The Environments\roblox-player key has (Default)=...RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe, baseHost=www.roblox.com, version, and clientExe. Bloxstrap's RegisterProtocol writes "<Paths.Application>" -player "%1", and Fishstrap's StartRoblox uses FileName=AppData.ExecutablePath with Arguments=_launchCommandLine.

One step is missing. The updater does not run in place. RobloxPlayerInstaller_EA24F.log (2026-10-23T22:00:08) logs 'Ready to relaunch: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\Roblox\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe -relaunch roblox-player:1+launchmode:play+...', then 'Creating client process'. A second installer log, ADA07, does the actual InstallUpdate. So the chain is client, then <versionDir>\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe, then %TEMP%\Roblox\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe -relaunch <URI with ticket>.

Also, Environments\roblox-player has a Capabilities subkey.
sources: local reg query of HKCU\Software\Classes\roblox-player, roblox, ROBLOX Corporation\Environments\roblox-player

verdicts.correction:
The BACKGROUND half is confirmed. Fetched today, GET https://clientsettingscdn.roblox.com/v2/client-version/WindowsPlayer returns 200 with {"version":"0.744.0.7441080","clientVersionUpload":"version-9ac8595712b447a7","bootstrapperVersion":""}, Cache-Control: public, must-revalidate, max-age=30, X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000, 5000;w=1, and Rbx-Cdn-Provider: ak. Log 8C675 shows updateRequired TRUE, then 'Update mode is chosen as BACKGROUND', then the join at +1.66 s. The installer finished at +10.76 s ('Installer thread completed successfully') and there was only one Player log.

Correction: the running client was 0.743 from version-11f155f3450f4c8e, which is where the Update thread started RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe. It did not run from 9ac8595712b447a7.

The FOREGROUND half, that 'closes every running RobloxPlayerBeta.exe', comes only from MultiAlt's launch.md ('Esse instalador procura e fecha todo RobloxPlayerBeta.exe') and was not seen locally.

evanovar #92 is a PR merged 2026-10-19, not an issue. It moves the exit decision to the existing 120 s startup deadline. It does not add a new re-binding window.

Local launch URIs carry channel:<name> whenever the account is enrolled in a test channel (seen: zintegration21, zintegration27, zfrmuncappeddrawdistance, ztm2-exp-a, zfullclientrecordingbuffertuningcontrol). That supports the channel-mismatch risk, but the risk itself was not observed.

The line formats are confirmed in the current log 8C675, for example 'web launch, websiteBTId is <btid>', 'BTID is overriden to <btid>.', 'Joining game ... place ... at ...' and game_join_loadtime with referral_page:RequestPrivateGame. evanovar's regexes are confirmed: browsertrackerid[^0-9]{0,32}(\d+), 'web launch, websiteBTId is (\d+)', \[FLog::GameJoinLoadTime\].*\buserid:(\d+)(?=[,\s]), and a plain substring check for challengedByGcs.

One claim is wrong. evanovar does NOT read open file handles. It lists %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs, keeps *_last.log files that are not CrashHandler and have a (\d{8}T\d{6}Z)_Player_ timestamp between -2 and +60 s of the process creation time, and then requires exactly one file containing the tracker. Process identity is (pid, create_time) within 0.01 s.

RAM's AccountManager.cs has no handle.exe or log-reading code. Whether RAM does this elsewhere was not checked.

Fishstrap's FileSystemWatcher (Filter='*.log', first Created event) indeed has no CrashHandler filter.

Note that web launches reuse the browser's own browsertrackerid: the same id appears in every local launch since July. A unique per-launch id is therefore RoALT's own choice, and it works only because the client honours the URI value.

The ActivityWatcher.cs constants and regexes match exactly. Its last commits are 02db760, 7dd22fd and ce723fc, all on 2026-08-05. Commit a9c193f0 (2026-04-04, 'Fix activity watcher when using RbxTransport (#6387)') changed GameJoinedEntry from "[FLog::Network] serverId:" to "[FLog::Network] Replicator created: ". GameJoinedEntryPattern still matches 'serverId: ([0-9\.]+)\|[0-9]+'. Log selection takes the newest 'Player' file created within 15 s, polled every 1000 ms, opened with FileShare.ReadWrite.

Locally, 'Disconnection Notification. Reason: 285' (19 occurrences) is far more common than Reason: 267 (2).

One correction to the design implication built on M11. 'EventWaitResultUpdate' plus 'Received close main window request' does NOT always mean another launch replaced the client. The same pair appears when the user clicks Exit in the client's own tray menu. In 0.737.100.7371443_20260917T111708Z_Player_D7A87 the order is 'Systray menu item Exit is clicked', then 'Main thread: Received close main window request', then 'WindowsAppReloadTelemetry EventWaitResultUpdate', then shutDown. In a replacement, EventWaitResultUpdate comes first and there is no 'Exit is clicked' line.

Bloxstrap 6ea198f1 is dated 2023-04-20, with the message 'turns out byfron will trip if you keep a process handle for robloxplayerbeta open for any longer than a minute'. It replaced WaitForExitAsync with polling Process.GetProcesses() every 1 s. Fishstrap still has the 'v2.2.0 - byfron will trip...' comment. Bloxstrap Watcher.cs polls GetProcessesSafe() every 1000 ms.

MultiAlt process.rs is confirmed as OpenProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE), then TerminateProcess(handle, 1), then CloseHandle, with PIDs from CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS). The PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION memory query was not found in process.rs and is unverified.

The Hyperion evidence is from 2023 and is stale. Exit codes remain undocumented.

The tool behaviours are confirmed:
- RAM (Account.cs, AutoCloseLastProcess) does CloseMainWindow, Task.Delay(250), then CloseMainWindow again with the comment 'Allows Roblox to disconnect from the server so we don't get the "Same account launched" error', then Task.Delay(250) and Kill().
- Bloxstrap Watcher.CloseProcess calls Kill() when force is set and CloseMainWindow() otherwise. OnAppClose calls CloseMainWindow and is attached only with activity tracking plus UseDisableAppPatch.
- Fishstrap KillRobloxPlayers is confirmed.

Two points are not confirmed. MultiAlt's kill_process in process.rs does not wait after TerminateProcess. The '1.2 s' wait in kill_for_user comes only from watcher.md and is unverified. The 'error 273' mapping is still unverified.

Caveat: the tray-spawn-on-close in tray-treatment builds was not seen in October 2026 logs (see M5), so 'expect a --launch-to-tray process' should read 'may'.

missed.claim: An official Roblox staff statement on multiple clients exists (May 2025). It calls multiple clients unsupported and says methods that do not modify the client binary are not hit by modified-client enforcement.
missed.detail: DevForum topic 3640609, 'An Update on Automated Action Against Modified Clients', posted by the 'Roblox' account (staff=true) on 2025-05-06, FAQ updated 2025-05-08. It says: 'If the method you are using to run multiple clients does not modify the client binary, then this change will not impact your workflow.' And: 'we do not officially support running multiple player clients simultaneously'. Modified clients include official clients 'modified by external tools at runtime', with action up to termination. This should replace the 2023 ScipioAfrikanos post as the primary risk statement in RoALT's notice. Note that MultiAlt's README claims 'Byfron has said multiple clients may be seen as suspicious behavior' but cites no source.

missed.claim: Named-object rules that change RoALT's design: names are case-sensitive, ownership is not needed, and the error codes mean different things for each name.
missed.detail:
Microsoft's CreateMutexW docs say 'Name comparison is case sensitive', and a local PowerShell test confirmed it: TryOpenExisting with different case returned False. Only the exact string 'ROBLOX_singletonEvent' matters.

What blocks the client is the type clash: CreateEvent fails with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE when a mutex already holds the name, also confirmed locally. MultiBloxy uses bInitialOwner=false, so RoALT can create the mutex without owning it. That avoids thread-affinity and WAIT_ABANDONED problems.

The design implication's error handling is wrong. For CreateMutexW(L"ROBLOX_singletonEvent"):
- ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE means a Roblox event exists, i.e. a client or tray process is running.
- ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS means another tool's MUTEX already holds the name (MultiBloxy, evanovar, MultiAlt). That is not Roblox, and multi-instance is already enabled.
For 'ROBLOX_singletonMutex' (a real mutex inside Roblox), ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS can mean Roblox holds it. Whether owning ROBLOX_singletonMutex stalls the client's waitForNewPlayerProcess wait is unknown. RAM and evanovar own it and clients still start.

missed.claim: Roblox writes the auth ticket in plain text to log files on disk, not only to the process command line.
missed.detail:
When an update check fires, the Player log line '[FLog::UpdateController] Update thread: start ""<versionDir>\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe" roblox-player:1+launchmode:play+gameinfo:<ticket>+...+browsertrackerid:<id>+channel:<x>+placelauncherurl:<...>' contains the full launch URI. It appears in 15 local Player logs. The updater's own logs (RobloxPlayerInstaller_*.log, line 'Ready to relaunch: ...%TEMP%\Roblox\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe -relaunch roblox-player:...') also carry it, in 23 of 38 local installer logs.

Implications for RoALT:
- Any log reading must redact gameinfo:.
- Never offer 'export or attach logs' without redaction.
- Treat %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs as sensitive.

The ticket's lifetime and whether it is single-use were not verified here.

missed.claim: Where tray auto-start is written: HKCU Run, value 'RobloxPlayerBeta'. A Roblox tray process can therefore be running from logon, before RoALT starts.
missed.detail:
RobloxPlayerBeta.exe 0.744 contains UTF-16 'Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' next to 'RobloxPlayerBeta' (offsets 0x71531f6 and 0x7153220), a UTF-16 '--launch-to-tray', and ASCII '[FLog::Systray] set auto start registry failed: {}'. Locally, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run has 'RobloxPlayerBeta' = 03... (disabled by the user) with a timestamp of 2026-07-22 22:31 UTC. The Run value itself is currently absent, but logs still say 'Auto startup is enabled'.

RoALT can read both keys (read-only) to warn that a tray Roblox may hold ROBLOX_singletonEvent at boot.

missed.claim: The tray menu's Exit produces the same EventWaitResultUpdate and close-request lines as a replacement, so those lines alone cannot tell 'replaced by another launch' from 'user exited'. Tray spawn on close is also not consistent.
missed.detail:
In 0.737.100.7371443_20260917T111708Z_Player_D7A87 (and in the tray process 30D25), the order is 'Systray menu item Exit is clicked', then 'Main thread: Received close main window request', then 'WindowsAppReloadTelemetry EventWaitResultUpdate', then 'shutDown: (stage:UGCGame)'. In a replacement (10630), EventWaitResultUpdate comes first.

No 'launched new process in systray mode' appears in any of the 40 most recent (October 2026) Player logs, even though all of them say 'Tray treatment is ON'. The last tray spawn seen locally was on 2026-09-20.

missed.claim: Reading command lines of RobloxPlayerBeta.exe needs more than a Toolhelp32 snapshot.
missed.detail:
CreateToolhelp32Snapshot or PROCESSENTRY32W gives the PID, parent PID and exe name, but no command line. Detecting '--launch-to-tray' or the browsertrackerid needs either OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) plus NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessCommandLineInformation), or WMI Win32_Process.CommandLine. evanovar uses psutil cmdline().

The command line contains gameinfo:<ticket>. Read it, extract only browsertrackerid and the --launch-to-tray flag, and drop the rest immediately. Short-lived query handles have not been reported to trip Hyperion, but nothing confirms they are safe either.

missed.claim: Launch URIs built by the website carry the account's channel enrollment, so different accounts can trigger different client builds.
missed.detail:
Local launch URIs contain 'channel:' values that change per launch: zfrmuncappeddrawdistance (Jul 28), ztm2-exp-a (Aug 11), zintegration21 (Aug 22), zintegration27 (Sep 17), zfullclientrecordingbuffertuningcontrol (Oct 9). Some launches have no channel at all. The same browsertrackerid is reused across all web launches.

So if RoALT builds its own URI, it decides the channel. Leaving channel: empty keeps production. This matters for MultiAlt's (unverified) claim that a channel mismatch triggers a FOREGROUND installer that closes all clients.
sources: local logs (UpdateController 'Update thread: start' lines, 2026-07 to 2026-10)

missed.claim: The updater relaunches itself from %TEMP%, which adds a process to tracking.
missed.detail:
RobloxPlayerInstaller_EA24F.log, 2026-10-23T22:00:08: 'Ready to relaunch: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\Roblox\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe -relaunch roblox-player:1+...' and then 'Creating client process'. RobloxPlayerInstaller_ADA07.log then ran InstallUpdate with BITS jobs and finished at +10.76 s.

A process watcher should expect RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe under both <versionDir> and %TEMP%\Roblox. Its command line also carries the ticket.

%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\LocalStorage holds memProfStorage13652.json (102,400 bytes), created 2026-10-24 01:00:08 local, the same second the client launched, and memProfStorageStudio8140.json for Studio.
